Reply with JSON only: {"verdict":"PASS|FAIL","findings":[{"id":"F1","severity":"critical|high|medium|low","file":"...","line":0,"issue":"...","evidence":"quote the exact code","fix":"..."}],"confidence":0.0}. If you cannot quote the code that proves a finding, do not report it.

AUDIT QUESTION: Batch 52 cycle 2 (verification). Cycle 1 C1 implemented: is_fresh mirrors the ledger's _aware ('Z' = UTC, no offset = not measured, TypeError caught); tests added.

Batch 52 = ORCHESTRATOR ORDER '01:55' item 1, on the word-pass worker (pipeline/word_pass_worker.py, merged in batch 51). The order, verbatim: "Make the word-pass worker take rows by published_at newest first inside a 10 hour window before anything older (ranked by score inside that window, L-u exclusions applied before spending GPU time)."
The change:
- is_fresh(row, now) is true when published_at is an ISO time with an offset inside [now - 10 h, now].
- pick() fills up to 40 in three passes, each in the adapter's rank order (score):
  (1) fresh rows, at most 7 per channel;
  (2) the remaining fresh rows, uncapped, so a capped channel's fresh rows still come before any older row;
  (3) older rows, capped.
- Done moments and videos with a full-video record are skipped in every pass.
- The cycle report adds fresh_h, fresh_rows, fresh_picked and fresh_channels.
- The L-u exclusions are the adapter's own (best_unused_moments drops hard flags, altcoin and speaker changes before the worker sees a row, so before any GPU time).
Measured now: the adapter returns 1340 rows, 78 of them fresh (10 h) from 7 videos. A cycle now picks 40 fresh from 7 channels.
FIND: anything still open; an older row before a fresh one; a wrong fresh / stale call; a test that does not test what it claims. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

+    def test_order_0155_the_last_ten_hours_come_first_by_score_then_the_rest(self):
+        import datetime as dt

+        fresh = [row(100 + i, 50 + i, pub="2026-11-13T01:00:00+00:00") for i in range(3)]    # ranked last, 5 h old
+        edge = [row(200, 70, pub="2026-11-12T20:00:00+00:00"), row(201, 71, pub="2026-11-12T19:59:59+00:00")]
+        picks, _ = W.pick(old + fresh + edge, set(), full=lambda v: False, per_cycle=5, now=now)

+        self.assertFalse(W.is_fresh(row(1, 1, pub="2026-11-13T01:00:00"), now))              # no offset: not measured
+        self.assertTrue(W.is_fresh(row(1, 1, pub="2026-11-13T01:00:00Z"), now))              # 'Z' as the ledger reads it

+def is_fresh(row, now, hours=FRESH_H):
+    """published_at read exactly as the ledger's own _aware reads it ('Z' = UTC; a time without an offset is not
+    measured, so never fresh: the adapter drops such rows anyway), inside [now - hours, now]."""
+    try:
+        pub = dt.datetime.fromisoformat(str(row.get("published_at")).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return False
+    return pub.tzinfo is not None and now - dt.timedelta(hours=hours) <= pub <= now
+
+
+def pick(rows, done, full=None, per_cycle=PER_CYCLE, per_channel=PER_CHANNEL, now=None):
+    """The rows to work, up to per_cycle, never one that is done or whose video has a full record. Order '01:55': the
+    rows published in the last FRESH_H hours come before anything older. Filled in three passes, each in the
+    adapter's own rank order (score):
+    (1) fresh rows, at most per_channel per channel;
+    (2) the remaining fresh rows, no cap, so a capped channel's fresh rows still come before older rows;
+    (3) older rows, the cap counting on."""
+    now = now or dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)
+    full, out, per, full_cache, taken = full or has_full_record, [], {}, {}, set()
+
+    def take(seq, cap):
+        for r in seq:
+            if len(out) >= per_cycle:
+                return
+            if r["moment_id"] in done or r["moment_id"] in taken:
+                continue
+            v = r["video_id"]
+            if v not in full_cache:
+                full_cache[v] = full(v)
+            if full_cache[v] or (cap and per.get(r["channel_id"], 0) >= per_channel):
+                continue
+            per[r["channel_id"]] = per.get(r["channel_id"], 0) + 1
+            taken.add(r["moment_id"])
+            out.append(r)
+
+    fresh = [r for r in rows if is_fresh(r, now)]
+    take(fresh, True)
+    take(fresh, False)
+    take([r for r in rows if not is_fresh(r, now)], True)
     return out, len(per)
